1: The diagonal of the rectangle is a diameter of the circle (an angle in a semicircle is 90°). Diagonal = √(3² + 4²) = 5, so circumference = π × 5 = 5π.
2:
For 1 ≤ x < 19, x − 7 runs from −6 up to (but not including) 12, and x ≠ 7.
• If −6 ≤ x − 7 < 0: y = 6/(x − 7) goes from −1 down to −∞, so y ≤ −1.
• If 0 < x − 7 < 12: y goes from +∞ down towards 6/12 = ½ but never reaches it, so y > ½.
Together: y ≤ −1 or y > ½.

DEF is equilateral, so ∠EDF = 60°. D lies on AB, so ∠BDE + ∠EDF + ∠FDA = 180°, giving ∠FDA = 180° − 50° − 60° = 70°.

The three lines make a triangle; z = 30° is one of its angles, so the other two interior angles add up to 150°.
x and y are each on a straight line next to one of those interior angles, so x = 180° − (interior) and y = 180° − (interior).
x + y = 360° − 150° = 210°.
5: Multiply the three equations: (ab)(bc)(ac) = (abc)² = \(\tfrac83 \times 12 \times 2 = 64\). So abc = 8 (or −8), and \(\sqrt[3]{8} = 2\).

I: f(2x) = 2kx = 2·f(x) — always true.
II: f(x + 2) = kx + 2k, which equals kx + 2 only if k = 1 — not always.
III: f(g(x)) = k(x + k) = kx + k², g(f(x)) = kx + k; equal only if k = 1 — not always.
So only I must be true.
